newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Defiant royalist Cambodian commander resurfaces.
newsitem.headline: Defiant royalist Cambodian commander resurfaces.

text.p: The Cambodian royalist party's top military commander, missing since bloody street battles in Phnom Penh earlier this month, surfaced on Friday and vowed to rally resistance against strongman Hun Sen.

General Nhiek Bun Chhay told reporters in this FUNCINPEC-controlled border town that he would fight for the royalist party until the end, and planned to combine forces and even negotiate with the Khmer Rouge to combat Hun Sen and his troops.

"I will regroup FUNCINPEC soldiers and the soldiers of our former allies from the KPNLF (Khmer People's National Liberation Front)," said the general, dressed in camouflage fatigues. "We (will) fight to protect the people and our territory."

It was the first time Nhiek Bun Chhay, former deputy chief of staff of the armed forces under First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, had been seen since Hun Sen seized power and ousted Ranariddh in a bloody July 5-6 coup in Phnom Penh.
Nhiek Bun Chhay led the royalist forces before fleeing their main military base near the Phnom Penh airport on July 7.
Rumours had been circulating around the capital that he might have been killed along with other top Ranariddh men, or that he had been seriously wounded.
He was among four FUNCINPEC men identified by Hun Sen as being responsible for the July 5-6 fighting.
At least two of the four were killed, and human rights workers said they were executed.
Nhiek Bun Chhay said he was not wounded but that his leg was swollen because he had been walking since fleeing the capital.
He said he escaped with the aid of some Hun Sen loyalists.
"I managed to escape from Hun Sen's execution because there are many people who still love and support me," he said in Thai. "Many of Hun Sen's soldiers supported me and helped me during the escape."
Nhiek Bun Chhay said he had come from the contested town of Samrong.

Royalists and government forces under Hun Sen have been fighting in and around the town in the past few days, but by Friday the town was under the control of Hun Sen forces, reporters who visited the area said.
Nhiek Bun Chhay, Ranariddh's main negotiator in talks with the Khmer Rouge before the coup, did not rule out the possibility of mustering support from the guerrillas.
"I will continue to talk with the Khmer Rouge to be allies in fighting against Hun Sen," he said.
But Ranariddh vehemently denied Hun Sen accusations that his party was seeking any help from the Khmer Rouge.

"I do not seek any help from the Khmer Rouge," he told reporters in Bangkok at a news conference on Saturday. "But I cannot prevent the Khmer Rouge from their own initiative to fight against Monsieur Hun Sen ... I do not ask any assistance from the Khmer Rouge. I would prefer a peaceful solution."
Nhiek Bun Chhay said royalist troops had not put up much of a fight so far against Hun Sen but they were regrouping and planning to make inroads.

"Many areas are still under the control of FUNCINPEC but the fighting was at a standstill earlier because there were no leaders. But one is here now," the general said. "If you encourage people they will have a fighting spirit."
A lieutenant colonel in the FUNCINPEC army agreed and said Nhiek Bun Chhay's appearance had helped boost morale.
"The general has given us a lot of willingness to continue fighting, and a lot of courage," he said.
Nhiek Bun Chhay said he was confident his troops had enough military supplies for several months.
Hun Sen and Ranariddh formed an unhappy coalition after U.N.-sponsored elections 1993 and the relationship had begun to unravel long before Ranariddh's overthrow.
The Association of South East Asian Nations has postponed Cambodia's entry into the group because of the political turmoil.
Hun Sen said on Friday the only role ASEAN could play in his country's crisis was to prevent foreign interference.
